overall: Violation found: the May 8 executive session lacked a proper purpose and was convened without proper procedure. Timeliness was upheld; intent, the June 26 session, and other allegations were rejected. Minutes release, training, and compliance ordered.

allegations.summary: Committee argued the complaints were untimely because the violations were discoverable at the May 8 open-session announcement; AG found all seven complaints timely.
allegations.key_passage: The latest complaint was filed June 19, well within 30 days of the reasonable discovery of the potential violations.

allegations.summary: Chair allegedly failed to declare detrimental effect in open session; AG found no required open-session announcement, no reconvening statement, and no roll-call vote.
allegations.key_passage: First, the Chair did not make the required announcement in open session stating all subjects that may be revealed without compromising the purpose for which the executive session was called.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the May 8 executive session was held without a proper statutory purpose; AG found neither Purpose 2 nor Purpose 3 applied.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, Purpose 2 was inapplicable to this executive session.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the Committee discussed topics not listed on the May 8 meeting notice; AG found discussion of outsourcing and cost savings went beyond the bargaining purpose.
allegations.key_passage: Purpose 3 limits discussion to those topics that directly correlate to collective bargaining negotiations, rather than broader policy or budgetary matters.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the Committee failed to create minutes of the May 8 executive session; AG reviewed existing minutes in camera and found no violation on the other grounds alleged.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law in the other ways alleged.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the Committee's violations were intentional; AG found the failures to take corrective action after the fact did not show knowing violation.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Committee did not act to intentionally violate the Law in the instant case.

allegations.summary: Vogler complaint alleged the June 26 executive session improperly discussed privatizing custodial services; AG found each discussed topic fell under a proper purpose.
allegations.key_passage: We find that each of these discussions fell under a proper executive session purpose.

allegations.summary: Complaints also named the Superintendent individually; the AG declined to review those allegations because the Open Meeting Law does not apply to him.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law applies only to public bodies and individuals acting as public body members.

allegations.summary: Complaints raised additional allegations that, even if true, would not violate the Law or were not timely raised; the AG did not address them.
allegations.key_passage: The complaints raise additional allegations that, even if true, would not constitute Open Meeting Law violations, as well as allegations that, even if true, were not timely raised.

remedy: Within 30 days, publicly release the May 8 executive session minutes without any redaction or withholding.
All Committee members must review the Attorney General’s Open Meeting Law executive session training video and certify in writing that they have done so.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be found intentional and may draw a monetary fine.
remedy_passage: we order the Committee, within 30 days of this letter, to publicly release the May 8 executive session minutes.
